title: Graded latency triage and capacity-quota router
creator: Aisha Nair
description: Design and implement a graded multi-region request router that combines latency-based routing, soft geo-pinning, and capacity-aware quotas to protect SLOs during regional degradation. Goal is to allow controlled, proportional load shedding and fast failover while minimizing cross-region latency impact and preserving priority user traffic.
context: We have seen two classes of incidents in the last 6 months: transient region-level latency spikes that cause global SLO drops, and slow capacity drain where oversubscription in a region causes high tail latency for new requests. Current routing is too binary (pin or failover) which either overwhelms remote regions or causes unnecessary global degradation. We need a middle ground that enforces per-region admission budgets, uses graded latency cost to steer requests, and includes per-region circuit breakers that trigger proportional shedding rather than hard ejection.
proposal: Introduce a scoring router that computes a composite score per candidate region: score = latency_penalty + geo_preference_bonus - capacity_backoff. Latency_penalty is derived from 95th/99th ms moving-window compared to SLO; geo_preference_bonus encodes soft pin (stickiness) tiers by customer/route; capacity_backoff is proportional to regional token consumption versus reserved quota. The router will allocate each request to the highest-scoring region subject to per-region admission credits. When a region's circuit breaker trips, it moves from normal -> degraded -> shed modes, each increasing capacity_backoff and enabling partial shedding via token-budget rationing. Also add a fast-soft-failover path that sends a small hedged probe to next-best region for high-priority traffic while remaining mindful of cost. Implement throttles at the admission controller to enforce budgeted shedding and preserve token-level accounting for cost and billing consistency.
acceptance_criteria: Router selects locally-preferred region for >= 90% of requests under steady-state with no capacity pressure
When one region experiences 2x 99th latency increase, global SLO (99th latency) recovers to within 10% of baseline within 90s using graded shedding and failover
Token shedding is proportional: at region overload, requests from P3/P4 labels are shed first with at least 70% reduction in their accepted throughput while P0/P1 remain >= 95% acceptance
Circuit breaker transition time and hysteresis prevent flapping (no more than 2 transitions per minute under noisy signals)
No significant increase (>5%) in average cost per successful token at steady-state after rollout
End-to-end automated test coverage for policy calculation and admission enforcement (unit + integration)
tasks: Design scoring function and thresholds (RFC) — Aisha to draft and circulate
Prototype router scoring module and unit tests — Jonas
Implement per-region admission controller with token budgets — backend team
Add circuit breaker state machine (normal,degraded,shed) and hysteresis — reliability team
Create integration harness to simulate multi-region latency and capacity scenarios — SRE
Add observability: per-region score, admission decisions, tokens_shed, and SLO attainment metrics
Run canary in west-europe with select customers and collect 2 weeks of telemetry
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math (edge cases: zero capacity, extreme latency)
Integration test: three-region simulator driving 99th latency spikes and verifying routed fractions
Chaos test: abrupt region loss and partial capacity drain to validate soft-shed behavior
Load test: ensure admission controller scales to 10k qps in dedicated mode
Cost regression test: compare per-token cost across baseline and graded routing under typical workloads
rollout_plan: Phase 0: off-by-default in staging, run synthetic scenarios
Phase 1: enable for internal infra routes in canary region (west-europe) with metric guardrails
Phase 2: enable for 10% of traffic for non-critical routes in production for 48h, analyze
Phase 3: expand to 50% with tuned quotas and hedging disabled for low-tier traffic
Phase 4: full rollout with SRE on-call and rollback playbook
monitoring_alerts: SLO drop: global 99th latency > baseline * 1.25 for 5m
Region admission budget exhausted for > 1m and spillover > 30%
Circuit breaker oscillation: > 3 state transitions in 5m
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive shedding might impact paid customers. Mitigation: priority-aware admission and explicit whitelist for enterprise customers
Risk: Cross-region failover could increase egress cost and latency. Mitigation: include cost penalty in scoring and tune hedging probability for P0/P1 only
Risk: Flapping circuit breakers. Mitigation: add exponential backoff and minimum stable interval before re-enable
Risk: Edge cases where capacity metrics lag telemetry. Mitigation: use short-term moving averages with conservative smoothing and safety caps
